Looking for our changelog for API/SDK updates? See here. ## July 30th, 2026 ### New connectors now available! Contentful: Connect directly to Contentful — your team's publishing destination for web pages, blog posts, and landing pages — so you can find, read, and update content entries without leaving WRITER. Instead of switching between your AI workspace and your CMS to look up what's live or make copy changes, WRITER works across both. Wrike: Extend WRITER across your project management workflows — giving it governed read and write access to Wrike projects, tasks, folders, comments, and approvals so it can plan and execute project work end-to-end, with Wrike remaining the system of record. Zoominfo: Connect to ZoomInfo's B2B intelligence database, giving sales, demand gen, and revops teams direct access to real-time company signals, firmographic data, and news. Rather than toggling between ZoomInfo and WRITER, account intelligence flows directly into presentation decks, emailed reports, Slack updates, and Salesforce or HubSpot fields. ## July 24th, 2026 ### WRITER Agent session logs and user feedback now available in AI Studio Admins can now enable WRITER Agent session logs and review user feedback directly in AI Studio, giving them visibility into how their organization is using WRITER Agent and how users are responding to agent outputs. Session records and thumbs-up or thumbs-down feedback can be viewed in-product and exported as JSONL or CSV for offline review. Learn more here. ### Analytics for Playbook builders In the playbook editor, we’ve added a new tab for “Analytics”. Playbook owners and collaborators will now be able to see metrics like runs, active users, and user feedback submitted via the thumbs up/down button. ### New Salesforce Connector is LIVE! Our native, WRITER-built, bi-directional integration is published on AgentExchange. Connect WRITER Agent to Salesforce to query CRM data, manage records, run reports, and automate workflows. Learn more here. ## July 13th, 2026 ### WRITER Agent analytics The WRITER Agent analytics page answers the most common questions about your AI program: Is adoption growing? Which teams are using it most? How much are we spending? What kinds of work is the agent actually doing? Learn all about WRITER Agent analytics here. ### Playbook reporting and governance: Visibility and control at scale Playbook reporting and governance gives you dedicated visibility and control over every playbook running in your organization, from the ones your team built to the ones other teams have published. Learn all about playbooks reporting and governance here. ### Skill reporting and governance Skill reporting and governance gives you dedicated visibility and control over every skill running in your organization. Learn more about skills reporting and governance here. ### Consumption data The Consumption page gives you near real-time monthly usage summaries and detailed cost attribution for your organization, split by user, team, and playbook. Learn about the Consumption page here. ### Our enhanced playbooks experience just hit open beta! The new playbooks experience introduces a redesigned editor and a set of capabilities that give you greater control over how each part of your workflow runs. You have until early August to upgrade and test your playbooks in the new experience. Once the beta period ends, our team plans migrate all playbooks to this new experience and deprecate the legacy playbook editor. Learn more about the migration here. Key additions include: Step reordering — Drag and rearrange steps on the canvas without rewriting instructions. Custom voice and instructions per step — Apply a different voice or a tailored system prompt to individual steps. Individual step testing — Test any single step in isolation to verify its output before running the full workflow. Testing with synthetic data — Validate playbook behavior using sample inputs without triggering live data. Reasoning and temperature controls per step — Tune model behavior at the step level to optimize for accuracy, creativity, or speed. Nested playbook calls — Call another playbook from within a step, enabling modular, reusable workflow components. Learn more about the transition here or get started with playbooks today here. ## June 25th, 2026 ### Admins can now create team playbook libraries! WRITER now includes the team playbook library to help admins organize and distribute playbooks across their teams. This centralized space provides governance and control over the tools your team uses to automate work. Learn more here. ### Pin your most used playbooks to the homepage Your WRITER homepage is now a personalized hub. Pin the playbooks your team relies on most, the ones built around your core workflows like content production, field marketing, campaign activation, and ABM personalization, so they are available the moment you log in. Team administrators can configure a standard set of pinned playbooks for their entire team in AI Studio, ensuring everyone has immediate access to the right tools from day one. Learn more here. ## June 22nd, 2026 ### Webflow connector now available The Webflow connector is now available in AI Studio. Connect WRITER agents to your Webflow sites, pages, and CMS collections to generate on-brand web copy and publish it directly to Webflow, deploy bulk copy updates across multiple pages and CMS collections simultaneously, and pull live content back into WRITER to audit against brand standards and compliance guidelines, with no copy-pasting or manual reformatting required. To get started, see Setting up connectors or take a look at our comprehensive dev docs here. ## June 18th, 2026 ### Admin can now customize the default WRITER Agent profile Admins can update the disclaimer language across the org by simply adjusting the default config. For more advanced or particular changes, they can continue to create a custom profile, which will override the default when deployed to a team. Learn more here. ### Playbooks can now be pinned to projects Add playbooks to projects so your project teammates have an easy place to find and use relevant playbooks. Note that any playbooks added to a project will be officially shared with project team members in a view-only role so they can run the playbook. ## June 10th, 2026 ### Export presentations to Google Slides You can now export WRITER Agent-generated pptx deliverables to Google Slides. This works similar as our Google Drive doc export and OneDrive export options. Your pptx will be added to Google Drive as an editable pptx. ## June 5th, 2026 ### Collaborator role now available for projects! Select between view only or collaborator access when sharing projects in WRITER. ### Admins can now manage presentation themes! In addition to personal presentation themes, WRITER Agent now comes with team and organization wide themes. Admins can now setup themes for their users to leverage when generating presentations. Learn more here. ## May 29th, 2026 ### Export deliverables to Microsoft OneDrive You can now export deliverables to Microsoft OneDrive using the same auth flow as MCP connectors. If you’re already connected, just select Export > Save to OneDrive If you’re not connected, you’ll see an OAuth flow pop up. ## May 27th, 2026 ### Semrush connector now available! You can now connect WRITER directly to Semrush's search platform. Query live keyword research, backlink data, and traffic trends right inside your WRITER Agent workflows to close the loop between search insights and content execution. Learn more about connectors here. What you can do with the Semrush connector: SEO content research: Identify high-value topics and generate optimized content to close visibility gaps. Data-driven briefs: Pull live keyword and competitive data directly into your drafts—no manual exports needed. candidates.usable_source_text: Alibaba’s open-weight Qwen3.8-Max takes on long-horizon AI tasks with 2.4 trillion parameters # Alibaba’s open-weight Qwen3.8-Max takes on long-horizon AI tasks with 2.4 trillion parameters View the LinkedIn Profile of Jonathan Kemper Aug 3, 2026 ## Key Points - Alibaba has unveiled Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter language model designed to complete complex tasks on its own over multiple days. - In testing, the model autonomously built software, reproduced and improved on a research paper's results, and successfully ran a simulated e-commerce business. - Internal benchmarks put its performance on par with top Western models. Qwen3.8-Max is available now, with weights set to drop next week. Alibaba's new flagship model Qwen3.8-Max is built to handle complex tasks on its own over days at a time, from reproducing research papers to designing chips autonomously. The team plans to release the weights next week. Alibaba's Qwen team has unveiled Qwen3.8-Max, its most capable language model to date. The model scales to 2.4 trillion total parameters, with 95 billion active per query. Qwen3.8-Max builds on the Qwen3.5 architecture, and the team says the focus is on completing complex tasks independently over extended periods rather than just answering one-off prompts. Alibaba first announced the model in mid-July as a preview version available through Alibaba's Token Plan, Qoder, and QoderWork at ten percent of the standard price. Even then, the team cited 2.4 trillion parameters and ranked the model just behind Fable 5, but didn't share benchmarks. Qwen3.8-Max is the first model in the Qwen-Max class whose weights will be made publicly available. ## Three autonomous coding runs put the model through its paces To show off Qwen3.8-Max's coding chops, the team presented three case studies in which the model worked without any human help. In the first, Qwen3.8-Max spent 16 days building the command-line tool oh-my-cli. The model took incoming user requests, turned them into GitHub issues, assigned them to itself, wrote the code, ran tests, and improved the results iteratively. By July 30, 2026, it had racked up 265 commits, 127 pull requests, and 151 issues, all without a single human touch. In the second case, the model received the research paper "Unified Data Selection for LLM Reasoning" but no starter code. Its job was to reproduce the paper's results and then improve on them. Over roughly five days and about 125 hours of compute time, Qwen3.8-Max wrote 7,600 lines of code and ran 33 GPU training jobs, according to the team. It first reproduced all six of the paper's main results. Then it tested 18 of its own ideas across four rounds and beat the paper's method on the AIME24 math benchmark by 2.7 points. The third case involved the WWW2025 Multimodal Dialogue Intent Recognition Challenge on Alibaba's Tianchi platform, where 526 human teams competed. Within 24 hours, the model fine-tuned several Chinese language models along with Qwen2.5-VL-7B for product screenshots and combined them into a voting system. Across 45 submissions, accuracy climbed from 0.60 to 0.853. That put Qwen3.8-Max ahead of 458 of the 526 human teams. ## Chip design and a simulated fiscal year test long-horizon planning Two more case studies target tasks that stretch across hundreds of interaction rounds. In the first, Qwen3.8-Max had to design a cryptographic building block for encryption schemes. The key efficiency metric for such a circuit is the number of logic gates it needs, the basic elements on a chip. Fewer gates mean a smaller, more efficient chip. The model started with a working but bloated design using 8,298 gates and whittled it down to 678 gates over roughly 500 iterations. After an automated layout pass with the open-source tool OpenROAD, the physical chip area shrank from 106x106 to 46x46 micrometers, an 81 percent reduction. The Qwen team says the model kept making deep structural changes even after hundreds of iterations instead of settling for surface-level tweaks. The second case study is E-Commerce-Bench, a simulation of an entire fiscal year in online retail based on anonymized data from Taobao and Tmall. The model starts with 100,000 yuan in capital and has to run multiple online stores in parallel for a full year. That means buying products, negotiating with suppliers in natural language, adjusting prices, managing returns, and dealing with crises like typhoons or supply chain disruptions. Hidden in the supplier pool are 152 scammers that the model has to spot. Qwen3.8-Max ended up with a balance of 416,252 yuan, quadrupling its starting capital. That's 38 percent more than the runner-up GLM 5.2 and more than 2.5 times what its predecessor Qwen3.7-Max managed. The model invested aggressively early in the year and pulled in a net profit of over 100,000 yuan during the holiday season. ## Multimodal skills and app reconstruction without source code For multimodal tasks, Qwen3.8-Max can process documents with over 200 pages and videos longer than 100 hours, the team says. They're also introducing RecreationBench, a new benchmark that requires the model to rebuild running applications without access to source code. The model can only observe the target app through interaction, meaning clicks and keyboard input. Testing covers Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Android, and the web. Alongside this, the team is releasing Qwen-MM-Plugins, an extension library that adds image and video processing, visual tool use, and multimodal memory to existing agent systems. Alibaba's benchmark results for Qwen3.8-Max across coding, agentic work, reasoning, and multimodal tasks compared to other frontier models. | Image: Alibaba In the benchmark tables the Qwen team published, the model lands near or above Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, and GPT-5.6 Sol across many categories. On PaperBench, Qwen3.8-Max hits 93, the highest score in the comparison. On TerminalBench 2.1, it scores 86.6, trailing GPT-5.6 Sol's 88.8. As is typical with self-reported numbers from model makers, these results come from internal runs. Independent verification is still pending. The Qwen team attributes the model's ability to sustain such long-running tasks to a major expansion of training environments during reinforcement learning. Training no longer focused on single tasks alone but also covered multi-day workflows, nested directory structures instead of individual files, and a variety of agent harnesses. The team's internal score index across more than ten benchmarks rose from 0.474 to 0.725. The model performed best at around 4,000 environments, after which scores dipped slightly. As the number of RL training environments and compute time grows, Qwen3.8-Max's scores rise steadily across dozens of internal and public benchmarks, according to the Qwen team. ## China's open-model race heats up Qwen3.8-Max's most direct rival also comes from China. Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 with open weights on Hugging Face on July 27, a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 2.8 trillion parameters and a one-million-token context window. Along with the weights, Moonshot also published parts of its own infrastructure, including attention kernels, an MoE communication library, and tools for running agents at scale. Independent testing tempered the company's claims, though. K3 fell well short of top Western models in both cyber capabilities and complex math. Qwen3.8-Max is available now through QwenCloud. The weights are set to go live on Hugging Face and ModelScope next week. The model supports both OpenAI's Chat Completions format and Anthropic's API protocol, so it plugs directly into Claude Code, Codex, Qoder CLI, Qwen Code, and OpenClaw. A parameter called`reasoning_effort` lets users choose between three levels that trade speed for thoroughness. Qwen says the model performs similarly across different agent harnesses and isn't tuned specifically for its own environment. | Image: Alibaba Qwen3.8-Max isn't the only piece Alibaba has added recently. A few weeks ago, the team introduced Qwen-Image-3.0, an image generator for information-dense layouts that handles inputs up to 4,500 tokens and renders readable text as small as ten pixels. At the other end of the scale, Alibaba continues to push small open models like Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, which has 35 billion total parameters but only activates three billion at a time. ### AI News Without the Hype – Curated by Humans Subscribe to THE DECODER for ad-free reading, a weekly AI newsletter, our exclusive "AI Radar" frontier report six times a year, full archive access, and access to our comment section. Advancing Toward a 'Global AI Hub' The key infrastructure that will determine the competitiveness of South Korea's artificial intelligence (AI) industry, the National AI Computing Center (KOACC), was launched with a spectacular fireworks show in Haenam, Jeonnam. The government and private sector are investing a total of 2.4 trillion won in capital, with plans to establish Haenam Solar City as a global AI hub. On August 3, at the Haenam Solar City Enterprise District in Jeonnam, the groundbreaking ceremony for KOACC was held with the attendance of major figures from politics, government, and business, including Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT Kyung-Hoon Baek, An Jungtae, CEO of Korea AI Computing Center (KOACC), Joonhee Lee, CEO of Samsung SDS, Congressman Jiwon Park, and Hyungbae Min, Unified Mayor of Gwangju-Jeonnam. At the groundbreaking ceremony for the National AI Computing Center (KOACC) held in Solar City, Haenam, Jeollanam-do, key figures from politics, government, and business stepped onto the stage and pressed a touch button to mark the start of construction. Photo by Lee Jung-kyung In particular, the event departed from traditional groundbreaking ceremonies. Instead of the usual “first shovel,” participants took the stage for a dynamic “groundbreaking ceremony” involving simultaneous button presses (touch button and movement), followed by a vibrant fireworks display—the so-called “groundbreaking blast ceremony.” This approach was praised for adding dynamic symbolism to mark the beginning of cutting-edge AI infrastructure. ### Site Area of 49,000㎡, Two Floors Above Ground... 400 Billion Won of Government and Private Investment Injected KOACC CEO An Jungtae personally delivered a business progress report at the event, announcing the official launch: “After meticulous preparations, the Samsung SDS consortium was selected in March 2026 as the preferred negotiating party.” According to the detailed business plan released on this day, KOACC is a massive national project set to be implemented over five years, from this year through 2030, with full-scale operation targeted for 2028. The total project cost amounts to 2,406.5 billion won. The initial core funding of 400 billion won is split between the government at 116 billion won (29 percent) and the private sector at 284 billion won (71 percent), establishing a solid foundation for public-private cooperation. The private sector consortium leading the project includes prominent domestic IT and construction companies, with Samsung SDS at the forefront, joined by Naver Cloud, Samsung C&T, Kakao, Samsung Electronics, Clush, and KT. The groundbreaking ceremony for KOACC was held at the Haenam Solar City Industrial District with a large attendance of key figures from the government, political circles, and business sectors. Photo by Lee Jung-kyung The physical infrastructure will also be on a massive scale. The center will be constructed on a land area of 49,053㎡, with a total floor area of 33,740㎡ (and a building area of 17,839㎡), consisting of two floors above ground. For the core power infrastructure essential to an AI data center, it is currently designed for a power demand of 40MW. However, a proactive masterplan is in place for expansion to up to 80MW to handle the expected exponential increase in data processing needs in the future. ### "A Factory Producing Tokens Globally"... Strong Synergy Anticipated with the Semiconductor Industrial Complex In congratulatory remarks and speeches, the guests all voiced their optimism about the bright future of South Korea's AI industry. Deputy Prime Minister Kyung-Hoon Baek emphasized, “The AI Computing Center will be a ‘token factory’ producing tokens for the world and serve as the cornerstone for South Korea to become an AI powerhouse.” Representing the private sector, Samsung SDS CEO Joonhee Lee pledged, “We will build the world's top-tier AI infrastructure and maximize the synergy from private-sector cooperation. Above all, we will create student groups that can grow together with the region.” At the groundbreaking ceremony for the National AI Computing Center (KOACC), key guests including Deputy Prime Minister Kyunghoon Baek, Samsung SDS CEO Junho Lee, Assemblyman Jiwon Park, Gwangju-Jeonnam Integrated Mayor Hyungbae Min, and Haenam County Mayor Hyungwan Myung delivered congratulatory speeches. Photo by Joong Kyung. Local governments, in particular, highlighted the explosive synergy expected from the integration of the AI computing center with the region’s existing advanced industrial infrastructure. Unified Mayor Hyungbae Min of Gwangju-Jeonnam stressed in his congratulatory address, “A 896 trillion won semiconductor cluster has been launched, and as you know, a national semiconductor industrial complex will be established at the Gwangju military airport site.” He expressed strong commitment to establishing the district as a core base through close linkage between the AI data center and the semiconductor industrial complex. Congressman Jiwon Park also noted, “Once the KTX and expressways are connected to Haenam, this will dramatically solve the accessibility issue and attract both companies and talent.” For a successful launch, Assemblyman Jungho Han of the National Assembly's Committee on Science, ICT, Broadcasting and Communications pledged, “We will provide legislative and institutional support by thoroughly addressing related measures, including electric grid separation, at the National Assembly level.” ### Hot Picks Today The Return of the “Solid One Home”: Non-Resident and Over 4 Billion Won Super-Luxury Assets Face Heavier Tax Burden [2026 Tax Reform] - "Why Young Koreans Love It: The Japanese Destination Seen as More Authentic Than Tokyo" - "Who Shows Up Like That to a Wedding?" According to the detailed business plan released on this day, KOACC is a massive national project set to be implemented over five years, from this year through 2030, with full-scale operation targeted for 2028. The total project cost amounts to 2,406.5 billion won. The initial core funding of 400 billion won is split between the government at 116 billion won (29 percent) and the private sector at 284 billion won (71 percent), establishing a solid foundation for public-private cooperation. ... The private sector consortium leading the project includes prominent domestic IT and construction companies, with Samsung SDS at the forefront, joined by Naver Cloud, Samsung C&T, Kakao, Samsung Electronics, Clush, and KT. ... The physical infrastructure will also be on a massive scale. The center will be constructed on a land area of 49,053㎡, with a total floor area of 33,740㎡ (and a building area of 17,839㎡), consisting of two floors above ground. ... For the core power infrastructure essential to an AI data center, it is currently designed for a power demand of 40MW. However, a proactive masterplan is in place for expansion to up to 80MW to handle the expected exponential increase in data processing needs in the future. ... In congratulatory remarks and speeches, the guests all voiced their optimism about the bright future of South Korea's AI industry. Deputy Prime Minister Kyung-Hoon Baek emphasized, “The AI Computing Center will be a ‘token factory’ producing tokens for the world and serve as the cornerstone for South Korea to become an AI powerhouse.” ... Representing the private sector, Samsung SDS CEO Joonhee Lee pledged, “We will build the world's top-tier AI infrastructure and maximize the synergy from private-sector cooperation. Above all, we will create student groups that can grow together with the region.” ... Local governments, in particular, highlighted the explosive synergy expected from the integration of the AI computing center with the region’s existing advanced industrial infrastructure. Unified Mayor Hyungbae Min of Gwangju-Jeonnam stressed in his congratulatory address, “A 896 trillion won semiconductor cluster has been launched, and as you know, a national semiconductor industrial complex will be established at the Gwangju military airport site.” He expressed strong commitment to establishing the district as a core base through close linkage between the AI data center and the semiconductor industrial complex. ... Congressman Jiwon Park also noted, “Once the KTX and expressways are connected to Haenam, this will dramatically solve the accessibility issue and attract both companies and talent.” ... For a successful launch, Assemblyman Jungho Han of the National Assembly's Committee on Science, ICT, Broadcasting and Communications pledged, “We will provide legislative and institutional support by thoroughly addressing related measures, including electric grid separation, at the National Assembly level.” ... With the government, ruling party, and local authorities signaling strong momentum by gathering together, attention from the business sector is focused on whether this mega-project, amounting to 2.4 trillion won, will proceed smoothly so that Haenam Solar City can truly become a 'global AI hub.'
